---
title: "Command line"
guide-section: "Guides"
description: "Convert between formats and parse model output from the shell."
---

The `cane-format` command has two subcommands.

## `convert`

Convert annotated documents between any two formats, including CANE:

```bash
cane-format convert corpus/ train.conll --from brat --to conll --on-conflict outermost
cane-format convert train.jsonl examples/ --from json --to cane-full
```

`--from` is one of `brat`, `json`, `conll`, `bioc`, `xml`; `--to` also accepts
`cane-base`, `cane-disco`, `cane-context` and `cane-full` (a folder with one `.cane` file per
document). The reading and writing options mirror the library's keyword arguments, for
example `--offset-unit`, `--scheme`, `--on-unrepresentable` and `--context`.

When writing CANE, `--on-mismatch` controls the parse-back check, and `--match`,
`--anchor-fallback` and `--prefer-whole-words` give the settings the output will be parsed
with.

## `parse`

Parse a model's CANE output for a text and write the result in any format:

```bash
cane-format parse output.cane --text doc.txt --variant full --to brat -o predictions/
```

Issues are printed to standard error, one per line, with their line number.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Success. |
| `1` | `parse` only: the output has issues (unless `--allow-issues`). |
| `2` | Any error, such as an unreadable file or an entity the target cannot hold. |

Run `cane-format convert --help` or `cane-format parse --help` for every option.
